gloss: namer; person who gives a name; name-giver

definitions.gloss: namer; name-giver; the person who bestows a name on something or someone
definitions.explanation: The individual credited with choosing and giving the name of a person, place, product, species, building, or other entity. Most common in news articles and official contexts (e.g., ship launches, new species descriptions, naming-rights contracts) rather than everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: この{星|ほし}の{命名者|めいめいしゃ}は{学生|がくせい}だった。
examples.english: The person who named this star was a student.

examples.japanese: {新種|しんしゅ}の{命名者|めいめいしゃ}として{記録|きろく}に{残|のこ}る。
examples.english: He will be recorded as the namer of the new species.

examples.japanese: この{商品名|しょうひんめい}の{命名者|めいめいしゃ}は、{当時|とうじ}まだ{入社|にゅうしゃ}{一年目|いちねんめ}の{若手社員|わかてしゃいん}だったという。
examples.english: The person who came up with this product name was reportedly a young employee who had only just joined the company.

notes:
Compound of {命名|めいめい} ('naming; to name') and the suffix {〜者|しゃ} ('person who does'). Literally 'naming person'.

USAGE:
- Most common in formal and written contexts: news articles, scientific descriptions of new species, accounts of corporate naming contests, and ship / facility launch ceremonies.
- In everyday conversation, people more often describe the action directly (e.g., {名前|なまえ}をつけた{人|ひと}, 'the person who gave it a name').
- Frequently paired with a specifier of what was named: {この{商品|しょうひん}の{命名者|めいめいしゃ}} ('the namer of this product').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新種|しんしゅ}の{命名者|めいめいしゃ}: namer of a new species
- {命名者|めいめいしゃ}{不明|ふめい}: namer unknown
- {命名者|めいめいしゃ}として{知|し}られる: to be known as the namer
- {商品|しょうひん}の{命名者|めいめいしゃ}: the person who named the product

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {名付|なづ}け{親|おや}: the one who gave (someone or something) its name — more emotional / literary; originally refers to the person who named a child, now extended figuratively to products and characters.
- {命名|めいめい}: the act of naming — the action itself rather than the person.
- {発案者|はつあんしゃ}: the person who came up with the idea — broader; includes but is not limited to naming.
